subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What name is given to a typeface that has no small strokes (feet) at the ends of its letterforms?
questions.explain: Sans-serif typefaces (such as Helvetica) have clean letter ends without the small terminal strokes found on serif faces.

questions.q: In the CMYK colour model used for print, what does the 'K' stand for?
questions.explain: CMYK stands for Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Key, where Key is the black plate used in four-colour printing.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is designed primarily for which output?
questions.explain: RGB mixes red, green and blue light and is used for on-screen and digital display work rather than print.

questions.q: In typography, what does 'kerning' adjust?
options: The space between individual pairs of letters
questions.explain: Kerning is the adjustment of spacing between specific pairs of letters to improve the visual balance of a word.

questions.q: A vector graphic is constructed from which of the following?
options: Mathematically defined points, lines and curves
A fixed grid of coloured pixels
questions.explain: Vector images use mathematical paths (points, lines and curves), which is why they can be scaled without losing quality.

questions.q: A raster (bitmap) image is made up of what?
questions.explain: Raster images are composed of a fixed grid of pixels, so they lose sharpness when enlarged beyond their resolution.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a logo in graphic communication?
options: To identify and represent a brand or organisation
To fill empty space on a page
To set the leading of a paragraph
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive symbol or wordmark that identifies and represents a brand, product or organisation.

questions.q: Why are sans-serif typefaces often chosen for body text displayed on screens?
options: They tend to remain legible at smaller sizes and lower resolutions
They always print faster than serif fonts
questions.explain: The clean forms of sans-serif faces stay clear on lower-resolution screens where fine serifs can become blurred.

questions.q: Why is a vector format usually preferred for designing a logo?
options: It can be scaled to any size without loss of quality
It stores more pixels than a photograph
It can only be viewed on screens
questions.explain: Because vectors are defined mathematically, a logo can be resized from a business card to a billboard while staying crisp.

questions.q: In typography, the term 'leading' refers to what?
options: The vertical spacing between lines of text
The space between two specific letters
questions.explain: Leading controls the vertical gap between lines of text and affects the readability of a block of type.

questions.q: Complementary colours are best described as colours that are:
options: Opposite each other on the colour wheel, creating strong contrast
Next to each other on the colour wheel
All shades of a single hue
questions.explain: Complementary colours sit opposite one another on the colour wheel and produce vivid contrast when paired.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of using a grid when designing a layout?
options: To organise and align elements consistently on the page
questions.explain: A grid provides an underlying structure that helps align text and images for a consistent, ordered layout.

questions.q: What is meant by 'visual hierarchy' in a layout?
options: Arranging elements so the eye is guided through them in order of importance
Making every element exactly the same size
Printing in black and white only
questions.explain: Visual hierarchy uses size, weight, colour and position to lead the viewer through content in order of importance.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of illustration over photography when communicating an idea?
options: It can show imagined or stylised subjects that cannot easily be photographed
It can only be produced by hand
questions.explain: Illustration allows a designer to create stylised, symbolic or imaginary imagery beyond what a camera can capture.

questions.q: Why might a designer choose warm colours such as red for a 'stop' or warning sign?
options: Red carries strong associations with danger and attracts attention
Red is the cheapest ink to print
Red is invisible at a distance
questions.explain: Colour carries meaning, and red is widely associated with danger and urgency, making it effective for warnings.

questions.q: You are designing a poster that must be read clearly from across a busy train station. Which choice is most appropriate?
options: Large, bold type with high contrast between text and background
Small, thin script with low contrast
Pale text on a pale background
questions.explain: Legibility from a distance is achieved through large, bold type and strong tonal contrast.

questions.q: A client needs their brand mark used on a tiny badge and on a large shop sign without any loss of quality. Which file type should you supply?
questions.explain: A vector file scales to any size without losing quality, making it ideal for a mark used at many different sizes.

questions.q: You are placing body text over a dark navy background. To keep it readable, the best choice is:
options: A light colour that contrasts strongly with the background
A dark blue only slightly lighter than the background
A colour identical to the background
A very small, thin dark font
questions.explain: Strong tonal contrast between text and background is essential for legibility, so light text suits a dark background.

questions.q: A charity wants a calm, trustworthy feel for its leaflet about mental health support. Which approach best suits the message?
options: Soft, cool colours with generous spacing and clear, simple type
Clashing neon colours and cramped decorative type
Dense blocks of tiny text with no images
questions.explain: Cool tones, open spacing and clear typography reinforce a calm, trustworthy tone appropriate to the message.

questions.q: You need to edit and retouch a high-resolution photograph for a magazine spread. Which type of software is most suitable?
questions.explain: Photographs are raster images, so pixel-based (bitmap) editing software is the appropriate tool for retouching them.
